The wheel came in on a Tuesday with a wobble you could see from the door.
I put it in the truing stand before I'd even taken the owner's name, because a wobble like that tells you most of the story.

Two spokes on the drive side were loose. Not snapped, just loose.
I've seen that a hundred times on commuter wheels that live on a rack outside a train station and get knocked by every other bike that parks next to them.

So I started with the spoke key and a quarter turn at a time.
You don't rush this. A half turn feels faster, but it pulls the rim past where you want it and then you're chasing the wobble from the other side for the next twenty minutes.

It took about forty minutes in the end, which is longer than I'd quoted.
The rim had a small flat spot near the valve hole, and I wasn't going to hide that from anyone.
I showed the owner, told them it would hold for a while, and said a new rim would be about ninety dollars if it got worse.

They rode off happy enough. I wrote the flat spot on the job card so whoever sees it next isn't surprised.
